title: Customs Borders
intro: Three international airport crossings: US→China (PEK/PKX), China→Vietnam (PEK→HAN), Vietnam→US (DAD). No overland crossings. US→China most complex; US re-entry most relevant for shopping strategy.

tables.caption: Border 1: US → China (PEK/PKX)
rows: Declare if carrying >¥20,000 CNY or >$5,000 USD equivalent
No declaration for personal-use laptops, phones, cameras
Prescription drugs: carry original prescription + doctor's note
Fresh fruits, vegetables, most US meat products prohibited

tables.caption: Border 2: China → Vietnam (PEK → HAN)
rows: Emigration stamp; carry out up to ¥20,000 CNY or $5,000 USD; VAT refund at PEK for eligible purchases
1.5L wine + 1.5L spirits; 400 cigarettes; declare cash >$5,000 USD
No pornography, politically sensitive material; no VPN hardware (software fine)
10–30 min for e-visa holders at dedicated queue

tables.caption: Border 3: Vietnam → US (DAD → US) — US Duty-Free
rows: 3–5% duty on next $1,000; higher brackets for luxury goods

tables.caption: VAT Refund
rows: Tax Free form at purchase → Customs stamp at PEK → refund counter before security
VAT invoice (hóa đơn VAT) → refund form → DAD airport counter
Luxury malls, Wangfujing dept stores — NOT Silk Street markets
Higher-end shops and dept stores most reliable

tables.caption: Purchasing Strategy by Country
rows: Silk goods, lacquerware, tea, traditional crafts
Collect forms at purchase; redeem at PEK
Tailored clothing, silk, lanterns, lacquerware, coffee

bullets.heading: US → China Protocol
items: Fill out Chinese customs declaration card on plane or at kiosk
Green channel (nothing to declare) vs Red channel (items to declare)
First-ever China entry: biometric enrollment (fingerprints + photo)
Immigration queue: 30–60 min typical at PEK; do NOT accept "help" outside formal queue

bullets.heading: US Re-Entry Strategy
items: Register high-value items leaving US (watches, jewelry) on CBP Form 4457 at departure
Declare all merchandise acquired abroad on CBP Form 6059B — gifts and commercial quantities included
Keep ALL receipts separated by country for Customs inspection
Luxury goods duty 3–5% above first $800; on $5,000 purchases rough duty ~$170–250

bullets.heading: Prohibited US Entry Items
items: No fresh fruits, vegetables, or meats (even packaged fresh products)
No live plants without USDA permit
No cultural artifacts without export permit from originating country
No counterfeit goods; no endangered species products (coral, ivory, certain shells)

bullets.heading: Cheapest Country by Category
items: Silk: Vietnam > China (comparable quality; Vietnam cheaper)
Tailored clothing: Vietnam (Hội An) — best value on earth for custom garments
Electronics: Buy nothing — prices not better than US
Luxury watches/handbags: NOT cheaper vs US authorized dealers

callouts.text: All 3 border crossings documented with duty-free allowances and restricted items
VAT refund process documented for China (PEK) and Vietnam (DAD)
Shopping likely exceeds $1,600 combined duty-free — register valuables on CBP Form 4457 before departure
Estimated duty on $3,000 above exemption: ~$90–150 — manageable vs savings; declare honestly
